description: The supplied image is not a scientific figure at all: it is the publisher's CrossMark "Check for updates" badge, a small raster graphic on a white background. It consists of a roughly circular ring broken into a yellow lower-left arc, a blue upper/right arc and a short grey arc at the lower right, enclosing a red pennant/ribbon shape that points downward. Beneath the ring, the words "Check for updates" are printed in dark grey sans-serif type on two lines. There are no axes, no units, no scale bar, no legend, no data points, no micrograph and no sample labels anywhere in the image; nothing is plotted, measured or annotated. Consequently the image carries zero materials-science content and cannot be linked to the paper's topic (a 3D cellular automaton model of dynamic recrystallization in low-alloy steel) or any of its variables. Panel inventory: a single unlabelled image component only. No numbers are printed, so no values can be reported. The only conclusion it supports is bibliographic: the article carries a CrossMark update-checking mark.

observations.observation: The image is the CrossMark publisher badge with the text "Check for updates", not a data figure.
The badge consists of a multi-coloured broken ring (yellow lower-left arc, blue upper-right arc, short grey arc) enclosing a red downward-pointing pennant/ribbon symbol.
The text "Check for updates" is printed in dark grey sans-serif type on two lines directly below the ring.
No axes, axis labels, units, tick marks, gridlines or coordinate scales are present in the image.
No scale bar, magnification value, or microscope modality annotation is present.
No legend, colour scale, data points, curves, spectra, maps, table cells or sample/condition labels are present; the image contains no quantitative values whatsoever.
The image therefore provides no evidence about dynamic recrystallization, the 3D cellular automaton model, deformation conditions, or any steel microstructure.
